ms.promise:
This is prototyping milestone. The goal is to provide the first implementation of TEE-based oracles on Cardano. The outputs are
・The instance of Intel Trust Domain capable of producing signed data for Cardano delivery and parsing
・The set of tools for TD attestation and verification provided by Quex
・Set of Plutus smart-contracts capable of receiving the data emitted by TD, storing it and providing the client contracts access with it
ms.criteria:
・The TD attestation and verification tools can be used to attest the TD in question
・The Trust domain source code is published
・Quex contracts on Cardano are capable of accepting and validating the data from the TD
・Test consumer contract is capable of fetching the data from Quex contracts
ms.report:
A. Output: The instance of Intel Trust Domain capable of producing signed data for Cardano delivery and parsing
Acceptance criteria: The Trust domain source code is published
Evidence: The source code of TD is published (https://github.com/quex-tech/quex-v1-signer/tree/plutus). And offchain part for data parsing and delivery (https://github.com/quex-tech/cardano-oracle/tree/main/off-chain). 

B. Output: The set of tools for TD attestation and verification provided by Quex
Acceptance criteria: The TD attestation and verification tools can be used to attest the TD in question 
Evidence: The source code of TD is published (https://github.com/quex-tech/quex-v1-signer/tree/plutus) and can be attested using the set of published Quex tools (https://verify.quex.tech/). All Cardano-related artifacts are available at https://github.com/quex-tech/cardano-oracle-artifacts.

C. Output: Set of Plutus smart-contracts capable of receiving the data emitted by TD, storing it and providing the client contracts access with it
Acceptance criteria: Quex contracts on Cardano are capable of accepting and validating the data from the TD. Test consumer contract is capable of fetching the data from Quex contracts
Evidence: The source code of the core contracts (https://github.com/quex-tech/cardano-oracle/tree/main/on-chain). Data delivery from TD to the blockchain together with its validation by the contracts (https://preview.cardanoscan.io/transaction/738ce1fc08f1fdbc5ba427c46ac392ac893918cc355ae8bddf62de72da5bf6af). Data consumption by the test client contract (https://preview.cardanoscan.io/transaction/51f1ae8c7e12a0a8df14002f87bdc5f8d9db1bbd7e0eb0da71df00511172371d)

ms.promise:
The goal of the milestone is twofold. First, develop the infrastructure necessary for data relay between Trust Domains and the blockchain. Second, develop the mechanics allowing clients to query the necessary data from the oracles solely by the on-chain requests. The outputs are
・The relay services providing the datafeeds for the testnets on a push-based basis
・The monitoring service for the on-chain requests
・Adaptation of the smart-contract code for the on-chain requests
ms.criteria:
The relays are not supposed to be trusted by Quex design. They are part of the internal Quex infra. Hence, we do not plan to make their source code public. ms.report:
A. Output: Security audit of the Quex smart contracts
Acceptance criteria: The audit report is publicly available
Evidence: Audit report (0 Critical, 1 High, 4 Medium, 5 Low, 8 Informational) and threat model: https://github.com/quex-tech/cardano-oracle/blob/main/audit/audit-376f9abd.pdf, https://github.com/quex-tech/cardano-oracle/blob/main/audit/THREAT_MODEL.md. We have reviewed and acknowledged the findings; in the current single-operator setup (the relayer is run solely by Quex) the residual risk is very limited, and the relayer-trust findings will be revisited before opening the relayer set to third parties. As a bonus beyond the grant scope, we also open-sourced the reusable audit toolkit used here: https://github.com/quex-tech/plutus-auditor
B. Output: Mainnet deployment of the Quex contracts and services
Acceptance criteria: The Quex contracts are on Cardano mainnet and the infrastructure is operational, serving pull-based requests with TEE-signed responses
